what: Review item R16-R21: E2E specs share and pollute seed data. The default Playwright config is parallel with retries, but the specs only work with one worker; the catalog's test-isolation rule (truncateTables default true) is for backend tests, and the e2e best practice only asks for TEST_DATA_PREFIX.
why: Specs were written for a serial run and rely on shared rows; the catalog e2e practice (prefix test data, clean up) was not applied to the webshop specs.
workaround: Logged for later; no change in review round.

what: Browser specs failed on helper waits: waitForResponse(/~get$/) timed out on the Shop settings row, and openAddAndApplyFilters hit a strict-mode error because two admin tables each show a Filter button.
why: Test design: the helpers assume one table on screen and a response for every click.
workaround: Waited for rows and used the filter helper per table; screen-based waits instead of response waits.

what: The F72 browser assertion expected one history row 'Status New -> Paid' after the webhook; the count was 0 while the status already read Paid.
why: Not explained in this chunk; the history label or the webhook history path may differ from the screen-based check.
workaround: Test reworked in the next round (not in this chunk).

what: A browser step waited for 'Operation executed successfully' after adding to cart and the message did not show before the timeout.
why: Not explained in this chunk; the add-to-cart success feedback timing or the card lookup likely differs.
workaround: Spec rewritten in the next round.

what: Earlier Playwright specs (levels 3, 4, 5) fail in 10 of 24 tests: the admin Products table shows 10 rows per page in database order and there are now about 150 products, so unfiltered lookups by name (adminReadStock, addFromCard, gridcell by name) and waits on the ~get response do not find their rows. The level 4 menu-order test also expects the menu from before round 15.
why: Shared dev database grew with seller and test data; the helpers do not filter or page; no cleanup or per-test prefix.
workaround: None in this round; GAPS notes it. Suggested: filter by name in helpers, prefix test data, cleanup.

what: Level 7 and the overhaul spec fail at random steps in some long runs (screenshot timeout, lookups not found, checkout response null), and pass when run alone (level 7 7 of 7, overhaul 2 of 2). Not proven to be caused by the checkout change.
why: Load-dependent: slow pages after checkout under a long session; no old build to compare.
workaround: Re-ran alone; GAPS records it as load-dependent flakiness.

what: Look spec failed in the dev run: clickMenu Quotes not found for customer1 (no company), and My returns was detached during a re-render (HMR) so the click failed.
why: Spec assumed menu entries that the test user does not have; no wait for the menu to settle.
workaround: Removed Quotes from the look list and added an order-detail screenshot step.

what: Seeded products were bought by earlier test runs and never restocked; Wool socks, Day pack and Water bottle were sold out and unrelated checkout and return tests failed. The builder added ensureStock (beforeAll raises stock through the admin UI).
why: Shared database with no test data cleanup for seeded products; each run leaves stock lower.
workaround: ensureStock(...) in helpers-customer.ts called in specs that buy seeded products (R16U-14).

what: Many specs depended on the generated grid markup (gridcell, row with aria-selected, columnheader, data-field, Number textbox, Rows per page) and broke when lists became cards; the builder rewrote 132 selectors with regex scripts and added cell, dataRows, emptyList and seekCell helpers.
why: Card lists replace the generated table; the old selectors are markup-specific, and the shared database makes the first page unreliable.
workaround: Helpers that match a gridcell or a shop-card; seekCell pages through 20 pages.

what: Several test assertions were loosened or rewritten to pass rather than to fix the cause: the returns stock check became greater-or-equal, the menu order test expected a new order (My returns before Return an item, Wallet added), the export date window was changed to 2020, and the notification check moved from a heading to a URL.
why: Reservation job and seeded data made the old expectations flaky, and the markup changed.
workaround: Assertions changed in place with comments.

what: Test race: addFromCard clicked add-to-cart and went on to the cart before the server answered, so cart totals were stale (13.00 vs 6.50 EUR, cart-goods assertion).
why: Spec does not wait for the mutation response before the next step.
workaround: addFromCard now waits for /ShopProductInfo/addToCart.

what: The reservation job (F73) cancels unpaid orders and returns their stock at arbitrary times, so dashboard counts and stock checks in other tests drifted by one.
why: Shared database plus a background job that runs during the suite.
workaround: Assertions compared with the reading after the order instead of before; stock check loosened.

what: After placing an order the admin dashboard 'Orders today' read 0 (the test expected before plus one); the cause was not established in the chunk, and the test then polled until greater than zero.
why: Unknown; the dashboard overview reads data through GenericProxyProps and may load late.
workaround: Expect.poll on the KPI tile.

what: Admin Playwright specs expected the 8 seeded products on one page; the shop now holds about 250 products, so 17 of 35 admin tests failed.
why: Specs were written when the table had 8 rows; the shared data grew over the rounds and the spec lookups did not page.
workaround: Added a seek helper that pages to the row; seed and checks use it; typing into generated dialogs verified and retried. Final admin run 35/35.

what: Specs with exact counts or stock readings flapped because the reservation job (F73) cancels unpaid orders at any time: F48 expected 97 got 0 in final2, F23 expected 57 got 58 in final6.
why: Shared, time-moving data; the job changes the day counts and stock between two readings.
workaround: F48 and F23 compare direction of change instead of exact sums; one exact stock assertion left in F23 and rerun green. Recorded as GAPS R16U-17, R16U-18, R16U-19.

what: Customer spec helper assumed the search box of a cards list is visible at once; cards lists show it a moment later.
why: Card layout renders its search after the page; a table has none.
workaround: Helper waits up to 4 s for the search box before continuing.

what: Other specs failed once on shared data or timing and passed on rerun: F36 coupon message not found, F37 sale price still shown, F44 export filter, F49 click timeout, F63-F66 filter button not found.
why: Shared data (sale windows, coupon states, slow pages under Docker load); causes not isolated.
workaround: Reran the named specs; all passed (7 passed in one rerun, F49 alone 1.7 min).

what: Shop tests change seeded product price, stock and names and do not restore them; ensureStock only raises stock.
why: Tests were written against a fresh shop; the shared data was kept across runs.
workaround: None; listed under not done in the round report.

what: Playwright install chromium hangs at extraction on this machine; the local config uses the installed Google Chrome channel and no retries.
why: Environment problem of the builder machine.
workaround: playwright.local.config.ts override (channel chrome, workers 1, retries 0).

what: The Level 9b integration suite took 158 s for 19 tests and printed large SQL traces; the builder read the surefire report instead.
why: Heavy aggregate queries in the test kit and HSQLDB logging.
workaround: Read surefire report.

what: Level 9b spec needed many fixes: missing waits for a field value, random SKU collisions, a wrong relative path to gen-import-products.py, a wrong file-upload selector, wrong column header assertions.
why: Test-design: assertions raced the background jobs and selectors were guessed.
workaround: Spec edits; screenshots checked; all 7 level9b tests passed.

what: Admin order view did not show the text Erased on request of the customer, so the e2e expectation failed.
why: Test assumed a UI text; the erased value is stored in the database.
workaround: Assertion moved to a psql check of the shipping address column.

what: e2e helper selectors wrong: applyFilter used attribute name name (menu shows Name); a Price textbox locator matched two fields because the read-only priceLabel field also starts with Price.
why: Test selectors written without checking the generated labels.
workaround: Attribute label Name; regex /^Price(\s*)?$/ and first() in typeInto.

what: Old smoke specs failed on the new paged shop home: S08 expects 8 cards with a description, but the newest seed products have none; the header search had to be used to reach products not on page one.
why: Shared seed data (50 000 products without descriptions) and newest-first paging; the old specs assumed the full list.
workaround: S08 sorts by name; showProduct helper in helpers-customer.ts uses the header search.

what: Level10b integration test: expected 6 units but got 7 (test count wrong, then changed to 7); then NoClassDefFoundError for PDFBox on the test class path, so the PDF assertion was removed from the integration test and left to the browser spec.
why: Test expectation counted orders wrongly; PDFBox is a provided dependency not on the integration test class path.
workaround: Count corrected; PDF check moved to e2e.

what: deploy/verify-restart.sh first printed SAME nothing was lost while the product create returned 400 and the admin REST path returned 404; the first login of the new user returned 403 and the new account count was 0.
why: Script checked counts only and did not fail on a missing write; wrong admin endpoint guessed.
workaround: Endpoint and description fixed; script rewritten to check the new account.

what: Push e2e expected HTTP 200 from the ship operation but got 204; test changed to accept both.
why: Operation returns no body; expectation not checked against the platform status code.
workaround: Expectation widened to 200 or 204.

what: Future-dated test orders (2097 and later) sat on top of newest-first back-office lists: F72 could not open its order; F86 totals collided with orders of an earlier run on the same days.
why: Shared data across runs; the specs seed orders in the same date range.
workaround: Random year per run; scripts/clean-future-orders.sql and cleanup in the spec.

what: The first Playwright guest check failed (test-failed-1.png) and passed on the next run after a 175 s wait, while the new Guest build was still being served.
why: Likely the check ran before the new bundle was served; not proven.
workaround: Re-ran after a wait.
